summary: This paper introduces Agent-Reflex, a general training framework designed to teach language agents to act reflectively under noisy tool feedback and user corrections. The framework consists of three stages: Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) to mine reflection meta-skills, Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) to internalize these skills, and On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) to provide token-level reflection supervision. Evaluated on six benchmarks, Agent-Reflex-8B significantly improves long-horizon tool use and robustness to interaction noise while maintaining stable training dynamics.

chk_data.paper_excerpt:
Corresponding author

Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon
reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to
correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery.
To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive
reflection in agents. Specifically, Agent-Reflex comprises three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill
Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capabilitydiverse LLM pool, mines matched success–failure pairs, and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills.
Building on this skill library, we then apply Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) that converts each skill
into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction, strengthening complementary
reflective behaviors. Finally, we propose On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) to combine agentic
reinforcement learning under noisy interactions with reflection-guided on-policy distillation to further elicit
proactive reflection. Built on Qwen3-8B, Agent-Reflex reaches 58.6 overall on five long-horizon tool-use
benchmarks and 29.1 on AgentNoiseBench, surpassing strong environment-scaling and reflection baselines.
Experiments on six challenging agent benchmark suites demonstrate the effectiveness of Agent-Reflex.
Further analyses show that Agent-Reflex improves agents’ robustness to noise while maintaining stable
training dynamics, supporting scalable agent training.

To address this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflective
thinking in agents. It models reflection as a learnable meta-skill: transferable meta-skills are explicitly mined from
execution failures and progressively internalized into the policy through verifiable reflection learning. Specifically,
Agent-Reflex comprises three components:
(1) Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD). We anchor 557 high-usage real-world environment themes and

automatically construct database-backed executable environments and tasks, injecting diverse tool-return failures
to emulate noisy conditions. From a diverse LLM agent pool, we sample trajectories covering varied task types
and response styles, and matched success/failure pairs are then mined into 1,170 reflection meta-skills across 557
environments.
